subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: Should OpenClaw keep probing macOS app-backed nodes for remote skill bins immediately on connect, or change the policy to defer/back off probes and/or skip only proven co-located app nodes?
rationale: Current main now implements macOS system.which/system.run handlers and docs preserve the node exec contract, so the unresolved choice is readiness and co-location policy rather than a mechanical missing-handler fix.

options.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
options.body: Delay initial macOS app-node remote-bin refresh until readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff while preserving valid node exec.

options.title: Skip Proven Co-located App Nodes
options.body: Skip only loopback/co-located app nodes when the gateway already has local shell access, while continuing to probe real remote app nodes.

options.title: Disable App-node Probing By Default
options.body: Make automatic app-node remote skill probing opt-in, reducing warnings but weakening default remote macOS skill support.

recommendation.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
recommendation.body: Delay initial macOS app-node remote-bin refresh until readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff while preserving valid node exec.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing candidate across the current remote probe, macOS node, and node-command policy history.
